audio_script_it:
Buongiorno e benvenuti all'aggiornamento finanziario di oggi, il vostro Morning Briefing quotidiano.

I mercati asiatici hanno chiuso la giornata con risultati contrastanti. Il Nikkei ha guadagnato lo 0,4% a 58.134 punti, mentre lo Shanghai ha registrato un aumento dello 0% a 4.000 punti. L'Hang Seng di Hong Kong ha chiuso in lieve aumento dello 0,3% a 25.947 punti. Questi risultati lasciano intravedere una possibile apertura cauta in Europa.

La tendenza risk-off continua a influenzare i mercati occidentali. L'S&P 500 ha guadagnato l'1,2% a 7.000 punti, mentre il Dollar Index (DXY) è salito dello 0,1% a 98. Il VIX, indice di volatilità, è sceso dell'1% a 18. I tassi di interesse continuano ad essere sotto pressione, con il TLT Bond USA 20Y che guadagna lo 0,5% a 87 e il US 10Y Yield che scende dello 0,9% a 4,2%. L'oro, bene rifugio per eccellenza, guadagna lo 0,1% a 4.800 dollari l'oncia.

Sul fronte geopolitico, la situazione rimane tesa. La possibile escalation del conflitto in Medio Oriente potrebbe rallentare la crescita globale, come avverte il Fondo Monetario Internazionale. Le esportazioni cinesi hanno subito un rallentamento a causa della turbolenza nella regione. Inoltre, le dichiarazioni del'ex presidente Trump sulla necessità di tagli ai tassi di interesse negli Usa hanno sollevato critiche, tra cui quelle della Yellen, che le ha paragonate a politiche da 'banana republic'.

Sul fronte macroeconomico, gli investitori attendono con ansia la prossima uscita del PIL QoQ Usa, prevista per il 29 aprile. In precedenza, il PCE Core YoY aveva registrato un calo al 3% dal 3,1% precedente. La BCE ha recentemente mantenuto i tassi di interesse stabili, con il tasso dei depositi al 2%. La liquidità globale, misurata dal Global M2, continua ad espandersi, con un aumento del 4,9% su base annua.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. 

Iniziamo il nostro deep dive con Bitcoin. La recente approvazione degli ETF ha portato a un aumento significativo degli afflussi di capitale. Nello specifico, il BTC ETF Daily Net Inflow ha raggiunto i 146 milioni di dollari. Tecnicamente, il prezzo di Bitcoin si attesta attualmente intorno ai 74.200 dollari, con una lieve flessione del 0.3% rispetto alla giornata precedente.

Passando alle altcoin, Ethereum registra un prezzo di 2.336 dollari, in calo dell'1.7%, mentre Solana si trova a 83 dollari, con una diminuzione del 2.9%. Binance Coin, invece, mostra una performance positiva, con un prezzo di 620 dollari e un incremento dello 0.5%.

Per quanto riguarda il sentiment del mercato, l'indice Fear & Greed raggiunge quota 23, classificandosi come Extreme Fear. Questo dato suggerisce una forte avversione al rischio tra gli investitori, che potrebbe influenzare le dinamiche di mercato nel breve termine.

Infine, alcune notizie rilevanti dal mondo crypto: SocGen ha lanciato una stablecoin conforme a MiCA, mentre crescono le preoccupazioni per una nuova truffa che prende di mira gli utenti crypto tramite un'app di note. Inoltre, si stanno formando nuove società di gestione di tesorerie crypto e Strategy's STRC ATM ha registrato un notevole volume di operazioni.

Grazie per aver ascoltato il nostro podcast finanziario. Per domani, tenete d'occhio l'andamento dei mercati europei e americani, e monitorate le notizie relative alle decisioni delle banche centrali. Un saluto da Prais Alért, e a domani!
audio_script_en:
Welcome to your daily morning market briefing.

Global sentiment is risk-off today, with investors cautious amid rising tensions in the Middle East and concerns about economic growth. The VIX index is slightly lower, but still elevated at 18.

In traditional markets, equities are seeing a rebound. The S&P 500 is up 1.2% at 7000, while the STOXX 600 is flat at 62. The Nikkei and Hang Seng indices in Asia saw modest gains, rising 0.4% and 0.3% respectively. In the currency markets, the dollar is steady, with the EUR/USD pair up 0.1% at 1.2. The Dollar Index (DXY) is also up 0.1% at 98. Commodities are mixed, with Brent crude oil up 0.8% at $96 and gold up 0.1% at $4800/oz. Bond yields are lower, with the US 10-year yield down 0.9% at 4.2% and the TLT Bond USA 20Y up 0.5% at 87.

On the macro front, investors are closely watching the earnings season and key economic data releases. In the US, the PCE Core YoY is due later this month, while in the Eurozone, the CPI and unemployment data are awaited. Geopolitically, the situation in the Middle East remains tense, with the IMF warning that a war in Iran could slow global growth to its weakest since the pandemic. The US and Europe are also in focus, with comments from Yellen and Trump's push to cut US rates making headlines.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets. 

The recent surge in Bitcoin ETF daily net inflows, with a notable $146 million influx, suggests growing investor confidence in the space. However, despite this positive development, Bitcoin's price has dipped slightly to $74,202, marking a 0.3% decrease. 

In the altcoin market, we're observing a mixed bag of performances. Ethereum's price has taken a hit, dropping 1.7% to $2,336, while Solana and BNB have also seen declines, with SOL slipping 2.9% to $83 and BNB edging up only 0.5% to $620. 

On the sentiment front, the Fear & Greed Index is firmly planted at 23, indicating extreme fear. This could potentially signal a buying opportunity for contrarian investors. 

Recent news has been varied, with SocGen launching a MiCA-compliant stablecoin and Pakistan relaxing its stance on crypto, allowing banks to serve licensed firms. Meanwhile, users are being targeted in sophisticated scams, highlighting the need for vigilance in the space.

Overall, the crypto market continues to navigate through a complex landscape of regulatory developments, investor sentiment, and technological advancements.

Thanks for tuning in, and we'll see you tomorrow. A quick look ahead: keep an eye on market trends and we'll be back with more updates. Until then, good luck with your trades. A final word from Prais Alért, have a great day and we'll catch you soon. Thanks for your attention and we'll talk to you tomorrow.

articles.title: The Bromine Chokepoint: How Strife in the Middle East Could Halt Production of the World’s Memory Chips
articles.snippet: The U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, now in an unstable ceasefire, has exposed a structural failure in the global semiconductor memory supply chain, and it is not the one analysts seem to be tracking. The story receiving attention is helium: Qatar’s Ras Laffan facility went offline, a 45-day inventory clock started running, and spot prices doubled within days. The story receiving almost no attention is bromine, and it is potentially the more dangerous one. articles.title: Hungary Turns a New Page
articles.snippet: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán conceded defeat in a parliamentary election on April 12, ending his 16 years in power, after his Fidesz party lost its majority in parliament. The center-right Tisza party, led by Péter Magyar, won and is projected to have a two-thirds supermajority. Orbán has been a prominent right-wing populist, with close ties to the Trump administration in Washington and warm relations with Moscow. Magyar campaigned on promises to address corruption, improve the economy, and align more closely with Europe.We asked five experts to assess how the election results will shape Hungary’s role in Europe and its relationships The post Hungary Turns a New Page appeared first on War on the Rocks .

articles.title: The Rare Earth Trap: How China Outmaneuvered the Entire Western Defense Industry
articles.snippet: In 1992, China’s political leader Deng Xiaoping made a comparison that should’ve set off alarms across the West: “There is oil in the Middle East; there is rare earth in China.” Instead, for the next 30 years, Western governments largely treated rare earth processing as low-value work — something they could hand off to whoever would do it cheapest. But then REalloys (NASDAQ: ALOY) came along with partners and started building domestic processing capability while most of the industry was still looking the other way.…

articles.title: Europe’s Electrification Dream Is Hitting a Wall
articles.snippet: The message given by Ursula von der Leyen to electrify the European economy is strategically coherent, politically appealing, and, on the surface, even unavoidable. It will be the real deal to decarbonize industry and power transport, reduce dependence on imported fossil fuels, and anchor Europe’s competitiveness. The latter is especially valid in an increasingly fragmented geopolitical order. Electrification is presented as the backbone of Europe’s future prosperity and security. However, beneath this clear vision lies a far more uncomfortable…

articles.title: Indonesia Turns to Russia for Oil as Middle East Risks Mount
articles.snippet: Indonesia and Russia are in talks on boosting cooperation, including through the long-term supply of Russian crude to the Asian nation, media have reported, following a meeting between the presidents of the two countries earlier this week. articles.title: China’s Petrochemical Sector Cuts Output as Costs Climb
articles.snippet: Chinese petrochemical makers have started idling capacity as the cost of their feedstocks rises amid the Middle East war, Bloomberg has reported, noting that output is down to the lowest in three years. About a fifth of the country’s petrochemicals capacity has been taken offline, the publication wrote today, citing data from a Chinese industrial news outlet. The report added that the petrochemicals industry is currently operating at just 68% of capacity. The futures prices of purified terephthalic acid, a chemical that is used in the production…
